title: Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little)
summary: Episode 7 of his channel-grading series, a 'Zoomer edition' scoring Lex Little, Max Euceda, Shizzy and Sam Sulek on 20 criteria out of 200. He argues the hate on young fitness creators is mostly jealousy, praises Max Euceda's education and Sam Sulek's character, and criticises bro splits, uncounted reps, circuit training and PED influence.
claims: He grades fitness channels on 20 criteria scored 0-10 for a total out of 200: programming, experience, integrity, usefulness, character, dogmatism, originality, black pill, humor, parasocial, empathy, god complex, production, science, clickbait, content recycling, conciseness, seniority, supplements, physique
Bashing Zoomer fitness creators as TikTok addicts who know nothing is mostly older-generation jealousy, not analysis
The Gymshark-era powerbuilding style of spamming compounds like sumo deadlift and bench is subpar for aesthetics; those physiques are a byproduct despite the method
The younger you start lifting, the more mistakes you accumulate and the more knowledge you can share; starting at 15 beats starting at 20
Integrity means acting in line with your own stated values, not with his; Sam Sulek never claimed natural so he scores high on it
Being sponsored by Gorilla Mind is a red flag for natty claims; he knows no verifiable natural sponsored by that brand
Older creators in their 40s clickbait far more than Zoomers, whose titles are usually plain descriptions
Advanced lifters are a tiny share of the audience, so beginner and intermediate content will always dominate
A natural with a strong physique who stays natural is a powerful anti-drug role model for young men
The only supplements worth anything are whey protein, creatine, multivitamins and vitamin D; everything else is a bonus at most
Shorts destroy attention span, but a 2-minute dip tutorial is far better than a meme short
Not counting reps is the easiest way to make no progress; tracking reps is essential for hypertrophy
Circuit-style training, moving straight from one leg exercise to another, is a cardinal sin of hypertrophy because it destroys performance
Creators who go against the grain and still get results are usually genetic or experience outliers, not proof their method is best
Childhood sport (peewee football, lacrosse) builds body awareness that later accelerates muscle building
Saying hypertrophy training can be whatever you want is false; doing whatever is why the average natural looks bad
He has subpar genetics and reaching 220 lb required paying close attention, not bro splits or doing whatever
Proper form is the cornerstone of any program; a great program with bad execution won't deliver results
Bro splits waste energy: six back exercises for 25 sets is wasted effort; 20% of that work would give about 95% of the gains
Consistency beats theory: a guy doing park push-ups and pull-ups with a rock backpack will outdo a theory-perfect lifter who can't stick to it
Beginners should get in the gym without overthinking; optimisation can come once you reach a certain level
The science-based lifting boom predictably swung the pendulum toward a new generation that hates science and just wants to lift; he wants a middle ground
Sam Sulek was doing lengthened partials before science caught up to them
Watching an enhanced idol tempts young men to think natural training is a waste and to jump on drugs, risking health and family
PEDs don't turn decent people into jerks; they amplify who you already are
Pro-bodybuilder supplement brands sell products unrelated to why they are big; $40 pre-workout is a scam, just drink coffee
The chance of looking like an enhanced pro with what they take is 0%; another reason not to do drugs
He grows his hair because he likes it long, not to copy Sam Sulek, and mocks fans who clone influencers
Final grades: Lex Little 122, Max Euceda 142.5, Shizzy 110.5 (after a black pill revision), Sam Sulek 127.5
